name: og-reproduction
title: Reproduction: Coupled Growth and Division into a Lineage
concept: How a self-maintaining protocell reproduces — metabolism-driven growth to a measured-geometry division with viable daughters, building a multi-generation lineage — one concept (Gate D), studied at several fidelities as arms: the coupled growth+division gate (og-33), the growth->division fate model (og-growth-division), and physical multi-generation reproduction (og-growth-alt).
gate_reason: Gate D (reproduction). This consolidates the growth/division line into one concept with explicit arms, each judged against its own matched null with input fluxes held equal: the coupled growth+division gate (og-33, canonical), the growth->division-vs-lysis/starvation fate model (og-growth-division), and physical multi-generation reproduction (og-growth-alt). Headline is bounded by the most-caveated arm: QUALIFIED — metabolism grows the compartment to a measured-geometry division with viable daughters and a multi-generation lineage, beating the decoupled/imposed null, on a coarse-grained geometry/budget abstraction. Each arm keeps its own verdict and matched null (see arms).
claim: A self-maintaining protocell reproduces by metabolism-coupled growth and division into a lineage. Metabolism drives growth to a division at measured geometry with viable daughters, beating a null where growth is decoupled from metabolism or division is imposed (og-33, qualified); net throughput grows the compartment to division rather than lysis or starvation, mass-conserved, where a no-throughput ablation does not (og-growth-division, supported); and a growing, dividing individual builds a >=3-generation lineage with volume conserved across division (og-growth-alt, supported). Headline verdict qualified (coarse-grained geometry/budget abstraction); every matched null and every arm verdict preserved.
question: How does a self-maintaining protocell reproduce — does metabolism drive growth to a measured-geometry division with viable daughters (not lysis or starvation), building a multi-generation lineage, each against its own matched null with input fluxes held equal?
hypothesis: Metabolic throughput grows the compartment to a geometry-set division with viable daughters and a persisting lineage; each step is demonstrated only where it beats its matched null (growth decoupled/imposed, no-throughput ablation), and coarse-grained abstractions are reported as such rather than tuned to a pass.
experiment: Run the coupled growth+division composite against a decoupled/imposed null (og-33), the growth->division fate model against a no-throughput ablation (og-growth-division), and the physical reproduction model to a multi-generation lineage (og-growth-alt) — reporting each arm's verdict + matched null with mass/volume conservation checked, and labelling the coarse-grained limits.

arms.concept_role: Canonical arm (Gate D, plan 33): does metabolism drive growth to a measured-geometry division with viable daughters, beating a null where growth is decoupled from metabolism or division is imposed? Realized: qualified — growth-from-metabolism to division at measured geometry, daughters viable, beats the decoupled/imposed null; qualified on the coarse-grained geometry/budget abstraction.

Growth→division fate arm: does net metabolic throughput grow the compartment to division (not lysis or starvation), mass-conserved, vs a no-throughput ablation? Realized: supported — net-growth-to-division, division not lysis/starvation, mass conserved; the no-throughput ablation does not grow.

Physical-reproduction arm: does a growing, dividing individual build a multi-generation lineage (>=3 generations) with volume conserved across division? Realized: supported — lineage reaches three generations, division conserves volume.

findings.statement: At equal feeds vs the matched nulls, the protocell grows from its own metabolic amphiphile production and divides at a measured area-doubling budding geometry with no imposed event. Division RATE scales with metabolic flux in the coupled arm (0.0125 -> 0.0500 as net carbon flux 3.36e-4 -> 1.16e-3; slope > 0) while the growth-decoupled null is flux-INDEPENDENT (slope ~ 0) and the imposed-division null divides on a timer (rate ~0.044) regardless of geometry. So growth/division is metabolism-driven and beats both matched nulls - qualified (met on the measured-geometry first cut, Option B). Guardrail: growth is funded by the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalysis.

Daughters resume the study-32 self-maintenance criterion (net amphiphile production >= degradation) across the flux sweep (daughter_viable = 1.0) - division is counted as reproduction because the daughters are viable (resume self-maintenance), not merely formed.

Division is triggered at a MEASURED area-doubling budding geometry (division_ratio 2.0; a proposed_input grounded in the hanczyc/budin growth-division geometries), not a tuned event - the coupled and growth-decoupled arms both use the geometry, and only the imposed-division control divides on a timer. Full coarse-grained membrane mechanics (viva-md-membrane) is the gold-standard follow-on (og-33a) that would re-test division under resolved membrane physics rather than a measured geometric criterion.

In the matched regime the internal autocatalytic source accumulates product, the osmotic pressure it generates draws solvent in, and the compartment grows to the division threshold and divides repeatedly (8 divisions over the run) — the chemistry changes the compartment's physical fate, a physical selection mechanism without an abstract fitness score.

evidence.observed: 8 divisions; outcome = divide; net growth sawtooth driven by osmotic pressure ~1.2e5 Pa

findings.explanation: OsmoticGrowthDivisionProcess integrates dN/dt (autocatalytic source − leak), Pi = R·T·c_in (van 't Hoff), dV/dt = Lp·A·Pi (solvent influx), and halves V and N at the division threshold.

findings.statement: Sustained net growth leading to division occupies a BOUNDED band of (network throughput × membrane permeability) — about a quarter of the swept grid — flanked by starvation where the membrane is too permeable (the product leaks out so the osmotic pressure never builds and nothing grows) and by lysis where it is too impermeable (the product is trapped, the pressure spikes past the burst tension and the membrane ruptures). Permeability, not throughput alone, decides whether autocatalysis produces a dividing protocell.

evidence.observed: matched → 8 divisions; too permeable (P=1e-5 m/s) → 0 divisions, net growth ~1.00 (starve); too impermeable (P=1e-10 m/s, high throughput) → lysed at ~1.5e5 Pa

findings.explanation: The equilibrium internal concentration scales as throughput / (permeability · area); below a floor the osmotic drive cannot grow the compartment (starve), above a ceiling it exceeds the burst pressure before division can relieve it (lyse).

findings.statement: The growth is driven by the chemistry, not by the compartment physics alone — with the autocatalytic source ablated (zero throughput) the compartment neither grows nor divides, while mass stays conserved across the whole cycle (residual ~4e-32 mol).

evidence.observed: ablation (throughput ~0) → 0 divisions, net growth ~1.04; favorable → 8 divisions; mass residual ~4e-32 mol

findings.explanation: With no source the only osmolyte is the small seed; the osmotic pressure stays far below the drive needed to reach the division threshold, and division halving conserves mass exactly.

findings.statement: A founder grows, divides, and its daughters do the same — a >=3-generation lineage forms in the agents map, matter and volume conserved at every division.
